11 1 Summary • The global extreme poverty rate fell steadily for three decades, from 43 percent in 1990 to 11 percent in 2020. This was an incredible accomplishment. However, progress has since come to a standstill. The extreme poverty rate has remained essentially unchanged after an increase during the COVID pandemic and the subsequent recovery. In 2026, 811 million people—1 in 10 globally—were living in extreme poverty, defined as living on less than $3.00-a-person-a-day in 2021 purchasing power parity (PPP) terms. • Extreme poverty is increasingly concentrated. More than half the extreme poor globally are living in only nine economies, and three-quarters in 20 economies. Of the nine economies, six are in Sub-Saharan Africa, where the extreme poverty rate has remained near 44 percent since 2014. answer: Năm 2026, 57% người nghèo cùng cực toàn cầu sống trong nền kinh tế FCS, tăng từ 12% năm 2010 [18c8b2db34697b7cf8bd8492dff472e8de71aeac90869187a1bc4febf6abfa75].
